ai.description: This snake reaches 50–70 cm. It is reddish-brown with a distinct dorsal chain-like pattern of dark-edged, pale crossbands. A V-shaped mark is present on the nape. Family: Colubridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Oligodon catenatus* is best distinguished by the distinct, dark, chain-like vertebral markings that form a continuous, zig-zag pattern along the length of its back.
ai.habitat: *Oligodon catenatus* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Chain-banded Kukri Snake is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice open reptile eggs, allowing it to feed on the contents.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon catenatus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon catenatus* is found in Northeast India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur) and the Eastern Himalayas, typically inhabiting forested regions at low to mid-elevations.
